pharm: A chlorofluoroquinolone formulated as a 0.6% ophthalmic suspension for topical ocular use; like other fluoroquinolones it inhibits the bacterial enzymes DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II) and topoisomerase IV, but is notable for balanced potent inhibition of both targets, giving broad activity against gram-positive and gram-negative ocular pathogens including some resistant strains.
quick: 1 drop in affected eye(s) 3 times daily, 4-12 h apart, for 7 days
Minimal systemic exposure; use only if clearly needed
Clinical response; signs of hypersensitivity or superinfection
summary: Besifloxacin ophthalmic suspension 0.6% is a topical fluoroquinolone antibacterial indicated for the treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis caused by susceptible organisms. It is developed exclusively for topical ophthalmic use (no systemic formulation) and inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV, with relatively balanced potency against both enzymes that contributes to broad-spectrum activity, including against some fluoroquinolone-resistant gram-positive cocci. The recommended regimen is one drop in the affected eye(s) three times daily, 4 to 12 hours apart, for 7 days. It is for topical ophthalmic use only and should not be injected or taken orally. Patients should not wear contact lenses while signs/symptoms of bacterial conjunctivitis are present.
indications: Treatment of bacterial conjunctivitis caused by susceptible isolates of designated bacteria (including Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Streptococcus mitis/oralis group, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Corynebacterium and related species)

dosage.d: 1 drop in the affected eye(s) 3 times daily, 4 to 12 hours apart
dosage.n: Treat for 7 days; invert closed bottle and shake once before each use

admin: Invert the closed bottle and shake once before use
Instill one drop into the affected eye(s) three times a day, dosing 4 to 12 hours apart, for 7 days
For topical ophthalmic use only - do NOT inject subconjunctivally or introduce directly into the anterior chamber, and do not take by mouth
Avoid touching the dropper tip to the eye, fingers, or any surface to prevent contamination
Do not wear contact lenses while signs and symptoms of bacterial conjunctivitis are present
moa: Besifloxacin is a fluoroquinolone (specifically a chlorofluoroquinolone) antibacterial. It inhibits two essential bacterial type II topoisomerase enzymes: DNA gyrase (topoisomerase II), which controls DNA supercoiling, and topoisomerase IV, which separates replicated chromosomal DNA during cell division. By inhibiting these enzymes, besifloxacin blocks bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination, producing a bactericidal effect. A distinguishing feature is its relatively balanced and potent inhibition of both targets, which broadens its spectrum and provides activity against some bacteria resistant to other fluoroquinolones.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to besifloxacin, other fluoroquinolones, or any component of the formulation
relative: Contact lens wear during active bacterial conjunctivitis
monitor: Signs of hypersensitivity (rash, itching, swelling, anaphylaxis)
Emergence of superinfection or non-susceptible organisms with prolonged use

preg: Systemic exposure after topical ocular administration is negligible, so risk to a fetus is expected to be low. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women; use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether topical ocular besifloxacin is excreted in human milk, but systemic absorption is minimal. Caution should be exercised when administered to a nursing woman; the low systemic exposure makes significant infant exposure unlikely.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed. Systemic absorption following topical ophthalmic administration is negligible, so renal impairment is not expected to affect exposure.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is needed. Because systemic absorption following topical ophthalmic use is negligible, hepatic impairment is not expected to be clinically relevant.

minor: Clinically significant systemic drug interactions are not expected because of negligible systemic absorption from topical ophthalmic use
interactions.alcohol: No relevant interaction with topical ophthalmic use.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference described.

serious: Hypersensitivity reactions including ocular and, rarely, systemic allergic reactions
Growth of resistant organisms or superinfection with prolonged use
rare: Severe hypersensitivity/anaphylaxis (as a fluoroquinolone class effect)
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with facial/throat swelling or difficulty breathing
Severe eye pain or sudden vision loss

monitoring: Clinical response of the bacterial conjunctivitis
Signs of ocular or systemic hypersensitivity reactions
Emergence of superinfection or non-susceptible organisms if used beyond the recommended course
counsel: Shake the bottle once before each use and put one drop in the affected eye(s) three times a day for 7 days
Space the doses 4 to 12 hours apart and finish the full 7-day course even if the eye looks better
Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean
Do not wear contact lenses while you have eye infection symptoms
This medicine is for the eye only - never swallow it or inject it
Stop and seek care if you develop a rash, swelling, severe eye pain, or trouble breathing
pk: Local antibacterial action begins promptly on instillation
Low systemic plasma levels; ocular tissue concentrations sustained
Tear-film/ocular residence prolonged; plasma half-life ~7 hours (minimal absorption)
Dosed three times daily over 7 days
Store at 15-25 C; protect from light; do not freeze
pearls: Developed solely as a topical ophthalmic agent - there is no oral or IV form, limiting systemic fluoroquinolone resistance pressure
Balanced dual inhibition of DNA gyrase and topoisomerase IV gives broad spectrum, including some resistant gram-positive cocci
Formulated in a mucoadhesive (DuraSite) vehicle that prolongs ocular contact time - shake once before use
Treat for the full 7 days; do not wear contact lenses while the eye is infected
Negligible systemic absorption means no renal/hepatic dose adjustment and minimal systemic drug interactions
For topical ocular use only - never inject into the eye or administer systemically
missed: If you miss a dose, instill it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule - do not put in extra drops to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Topical ophthalmic overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity given negligible absorption. A single accidental dose may be flushed from the eye(s) with lukewarm water. Accidental oral ingestion of the small volume in the bottle is not expected to cause serious harm; manage supportively.
